title: A Shield Around Me: David Flees from Absalom
summary: Headed as a psalm of David from the time he fled from his son Absalom, this prayer begins with enemies multiplying and voices saying God will not rescue him. David answers that the LORD is his shield, his glory, and the one who lifts his head; he cries out and God answers from his holy mountain. Having slept and woken safely, he refuses to fear the thousands against him, calls on God to rise and save, and closes by declaring that salvation belongs to the LORD, with a blessing on God's people.

from.where: The Study Bible's notes on Psalm 3

line: David, fleeing his own son, hears voices say God will not rescue him, answers that the LORD is his shield, and lies down and wakes again in safety.
guide: Notice the voice that says God will not deliver you, and make the psalm's turn: stop arguing with it and speak to God instead. Tonight, name to God what you fear and hand it over. The psalm ends by saying that salvation is the LORD's work, not yours.

care.text: The harder curses in the Psalms, and the main ways Christians have read them, are set out in the part on the cursing psalms on the book page. None of those readings gives anyone permission to harm another person.

stanzas.title: The LORD, a shield who answers from his holy mountain
Arise, O LORD: salvation belongs to you

verses.t: A Psalm of David, when he fled from his son Absalom. O LORD, how my foes have increased! How many rise up against me!
Many say of me, “God will not deliver him.” Selah
But You, O LORD, are a shield around me, my glory, and the One who lifts my head.
To the LORD I cry aloud, and He answers me from His holy mountain. Selah
I lie down and sleep; I wake again, for the LORD sustains me.
I will not fear the myriads set against me on every side.
Arise, O LORD! Save me, O my God! Strike all my enemies on the jaw; break the teeth of the wicked.
Salvation belongs to the LORD; may Your blessing be on Your people. Selah
